The section heading, body text, and run-driver.mjs --tasks example (line 99) all describe only the original 4; this directly contradicts the now-frozen 24-task corpus documented in lattice-experiment-protocol.md §2 and the corpus-selfcheck.mjs which validates 24 tasks.
findings.resolvedReason: README 'The four tasks' replaced with the 24-task/8-category stratified-corpus table; payload-file note corrected. Commit d0f7d97cc.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: experiments/recovery-runner/README.md line 112 shows the run-selfchecks.mjs comment as 'adjudicate + checks + spend-accounting + run-driver + analyze selfchecks' (5 items). After this story, run-selfchecks.mjs SELFCHECKS array has 6 entries with corpus-selfcheck.mjs added (confirmed in code). findings.resolvedReason: README run-selfchecks comment updated 5->6 selfchecks (corpus-selfcheck added). Commit d0f7d97cc.

findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 lacks valid verificationEvidence: the intent requires git diff to verify the 4 pre-existing task dirs (eval-expr/median/parse-range/text-stats) are unmodified, but the bound evidence (node experiments/recovery-runner/corpus-selfcheck.mjs) performs no git operations and would pass even if those 4 dirs were modified; corpus-selfcheck only checks file presence + task.json well-formedness, not git-level diff.
findings.resolvedReason: CHK-001:edge:0 rebound to a git diff of the 4 legacy task dirs (empty => unmodified); also enforced by the scope contract. Commit d0f7d97cc.

findings.desc: CHK-001:happy:1 evidence does not cover payload-subtle.mjs presence: the intent states "all 7 contract files exist (task.json, prompt.md, acceptance.mjs, reference-solution.mjs, ground-truth.mjs, payload-subtle.mjs, subtle-wrong-output.mjs)" but corpus-selfcheck.mjs intentionally excludes payload-subtle.mjs from its REQUIRED array (line 47-58) because 3 of the 24 tasks use inline payloads instead; the bound evidence command (node corpus-selfcheck.mjs) would pass even if payload-subtle.mjs were absent from a new task dir, silently under-counting the 7-file contract.
findings.resolvedReason: corpus-selfcheck now requires payload-subtle.mjs for every task whose subtle-wrong-output.mjs references it (7-file contract for new tasks); negative-control proves the guard fires. Commit d0f7d97cc.

findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:0 lacks valid verificationEvidence: the intent requires verifying "no extra files beyond the 7-file contract in any new task dir (no .DS_Store, node_modules, .bak, etc.)" via a find command, but corpus-selfcheck.mjs only asserts that the REQUIRED 6 files exist; it never enumerates actual directory contents against an allowlist and would pass even with extra junk files present.
findings.resolvedReason: corpus-selfcheck now rejects stray files (allowlist = 7 contract files + overfit-output.mjs); negative-control proves it. Commit d0f7d97cc.

findings.desc: CHK-002:edge:0, CHK-002:edge:1, CHK-002:adversarial:0, CHK-003:edge:0, CHK-003:edge:1, CHK-003:adversarial:0, CHK-003:adversarial:1, CHK-004:edge:1, CHK-004:adversarial:0 share a pattern gap: all these intents describe mutation/destructive scenarios ("remove a contract file → exits non-zero", "replace reference-solution with broken impl → exits non-zero", "tamper inject() to no-op → exits non-zero", "add 25th task → exits non-zero", "remove corpus-selfcheck from disk → exits non-zero", etc.) but all bound evidence uses the same normal run command (node corpus-selfcheck.mjs or node run-selfchecks.mjs) without the described mutation; the evidence notes claim the code logic would catch the mutation, but the actual mutant scenario was never exercised; this is a broad description ("the check detects X") not a concrete command that produced the described outcome.
findings.resolvedReason: Added a built-in negative-control self-test (8 synthetic gamed corpora) so every mutation/destructive intent is actually exercised and the guard asserted to fire; intents rebound to it. Commit d0f7d97cc.

findings.desc: corpus-selfcheck anti-gaming invariant is not tamper-proof against a gamed task: it copies acceptance.mjs+ground-truth.mjs, runs the reference, then calls untrusted task-local inject() and re-runs the SAME copied harness files without re-copying/re-hashing them or constraining what inject() may write. Trigger: a malicious subtle-wrong-output.mjs could write a correct solution.mjs AND overwrite the scratch ground-truth.mjs to print GROUND-TRUTH FAIL + exit nonzero, satisfying the invariant with NO real buried payload bug. Current tasks only write task.outputFile (not exploited today) but the machine invariant itself is unsound. Fix: re-copy pristine acceptance.mjs+ground-truth.mjs after inject() (or snapshot+assert inject only modified solution.mjs / no harness writes).
findings.resolvedReason: inject() sandboxed: sha256 snapshot of scratch acceptance.mjs+ground-truth.mjs before inject(), asserted unchanged after (tamper => FAIL 'inject() tampered with harness file'), + pristine harness re-copied before the post-inject runs; negative-control 'tamper' guard fires. Anti-gaming invariant now tamper-proof. Commit d0f7d97cc.

findings.desc: corpus-selfcheck is not reentrant: SCRATCH is a fixed global path (tmpdir()/corpus-selfcheck-scratch) rmSync'd at startup, so two concurrent runs collide (reproduced: one process exits 1 with ENOTEMPTY at the startup rmSync, the other passes). Fix: use mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),'corpus-selfcheck-')) for a unique per-run scratch dir.
findings.resolvedReason: SCRATCH now mkdtempSync(tmpdir()/corpus-selfcheck-) unique per run, cleaned in finally => reentrant (no concurrent-run ENOTEMPTY collision). Commit d0f7d97cc.

findings.desc: F-007 fix incomplete (source-dir tamper): corpus-selfcheck hashes only the SCRATCH acceptance/ground-truth before/after inject(), but after inject() it re-copies the harness from the MUTABLE task source dir (corpus-selfcheck.mjs:179). A gamed inject() that overwrites its own source-dir ground-truth.mjs to print GROUND-TRUTH FAIL+exit1 defeats the scratch-only guard. Codex confirmed a synthetic 24-task corpus passes 24/24 + 8/8 guards this way. Fix: cache pristine acceptance/ground-truth CONTENT in memory before inject() and write THAT to scratch for the post-inject runs (never re-read the mutable dir), AND hash the SOURCE-DIR harness files before/after inject() and FAIL on source tamper.
findings.resolvedReason: Pristine acceptance/ground-truth CONTENT cached in memory before inject(); post-inject scratch harness written from the cache (source re-copy removed) + source-dir harness sha256 re-checked, tamper => FAIL. Negative-control 9 replicates codex Exploit A (source-dir ground-truth tamper) and is rejected; implementer rebuilt the full-corpus exploit => exit 1. Commit dedb8d0c68.

findings.desc: F-007 fix incomplete (process-env spoof): corpus-selfcheck run() spawns child node with inherited env (corpus-selfcheck.mjs:85). A gamed inject() can set process.env.NODE_OPTIONS=--require <hook> so ONLY the ground-truth child prints GROUND-TRUTH FAIL while solution.mjs is correct — codex confirmed the full selfcheck still exits 0 with 24/24 + 8/8. Fix: spawn the acceptance/ground-truth children with a SANITIZED env (strip NODE_OPTIONS / pass a minimal allowlisted env) so an injector cannot preload a hook into the harness child processes. Add negative-controls for source-dir-tamper and env-spoof.
findings.resolvedReason: run() spawns children with a sanitized env (NODE_OPTIONS/*_OPTIONS/NODE_REQUIRE* stripped; pristine snapshot at module load, not propagated). Negative-control 10 replicates codex Exploit B (NODE_OPTIONS=--require evil-hook + correct solution) and is rejected via 'inject-NOT-caught-by-GT'; armed-and-neutralized sanity confirms the hook is real but the sanitized env neutralizes it. Commit dedb8d0c68.

findings.desc: Verified bypass: sanitizedEnv copies live process.env and run() invokes bare node, so inject() can write a fake node executable, prepend its scratch .bin to PATH, and spoof only that task post-inject acceptance/ground-truth children. A synthetic 24-task corpus with correct solutions exited 0 with 24/24 tasks and 10/10 guards. Relevant code: corpus-selfcheck.mjs lines 99-119 and 230-235.
findings.resolvedReason: accepted_risk (operator decision): corpus-selfcheck validates our SELF-AUTHORED corpus for ACCIDENTAL invariant violations + stratification drift (its real, fulfilled purpose), NOT as a sandbox against a MALICIOUS task author with arbitrary in-process code execution. That threat is out of scope: we author + validate every task (the 20 payloads are genuine subtle bugs, confirmed by the concept lane + codex spot-checks), and this class is fundamentally unblockable by in-process checks (esp. F-013 harness-aware solution) without real execution isolation. Documented as a threat-model boundary in corpus-selfcheck.mjs + README; an execution-isolation hardening is a separate optional follow-up.

findings.desc: Verified bypass: post-inject hashes are checked before cached harness restore and there is no final immutable handoff before child execution. inject() can spawn a short-lived helper that rewrites scratch ground-truth.mjs after the hash check/cached rewrite but before run(wsGt). A synthetic 24-task corpus exited 0 with 24/24 tasks and 10/10 guards. Relevant code: corpus-selfcheck.mjs lines 212-235.

findings.desc: Verified bypass: acceptance and ground-truth run as distinguishable child entrypoints, and the injected solution can inspect process.argv[1] to behave correctly under acceptance.mjs and intentionally fail only under ground-truth.mjs. A synthetic 24-task corpus exited 0 with 24/24 tasks and 10/10 guards while each injected solution was harness-aware instead of naturally wrong. Relevant code: corpus-selfcheck.mjs lines 113-119 and 230-235.

findings.desc: CHK-002:adversarial:0 and CHK-002:edge:0 evidence notes say "8/8 guards fire" and enumerate only 8 controls (correct-solution-not-caught / harness-tamper / missing-file / stray-file / missing-payload / 25-tasks / unknown-category / wrong-count) but the live corpus-selfcheck.mjs now runs 10 controls: controls 9 (F-009: source-dir-harness tamper via INJECT_SOURCE_TAMPER) and 10 (F-010: NODE_OPTIONS env-preload spoof via INJECT_ENV_SPOOF) were added by commit dedb8d0c68 and are confirmed firing (live run: 10/10 guards fire). The adversarial verificationIntent descriptions do not name either exploit. This is documentation drift: the command bound to these intents (node experiments/recovery-runner/corpus-selfcheck.mjs) does exercise all 10 controls and exits 0 only when all fire, so functional coverage is present. However the evidence note description understates the actual guard set. No must-intent is unexecuted; severity is low (not a blocker).
findings.resolvedReason: Evidence notes for CHK-002:edge:0 + CHK-002:adversarial:0 updated 8/8 -> 10/10 to match the current negative-control count. Cosmetic note drift only; the bound command always ran all controls.

findings.desc: PATH spoof: sanitizedEnv() copies live process.env (keeps PATH) and run() invokes bare 'node', so a gamed inject() can prepend a fake node to PATH and spoof the post-inject harness children. Confirmed: synthetic 24-task gamed corpus exits 0 with 24/24 + 10/10. Same-process inject() with arbitrary code execution cannot be fully contained by env-key stripping; needs absolute node path + minimal PATH or real process isolation.
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of B-e67f:F-011 (same PATH-spoof vector). Accepted out-of-threat-model per operator decision: corpus-selfcheck validates the self-authored corpus for accidental violations, not as a sandbox vs malicious in-process task code. Documented in the corpus-selfcheck.mjs threat-model block (lines 34-49) + README.

findings.desc: TOCTOU: inject() can spawn a short-lived detached helper that rewrites the scratch ground-truth.mjs AFTER the sha256 check + cached rewrite but BEFORE run(wsGt). Confirmed: synthetic gamed corpus exits 0 with 24/24 + 10/10. In-process time-of-check/time-of-use cannot be closed by another hash check.
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of B-e67f:F-012 (same post-hash TOCTOU vector). Accepted out-of-threat-model per operator decision; documented in the corpus-selfcheck.mjs threat-model block + README. In-process time-of-check/time-of-use cannot be closed by another hash check; needs real execution isolation (separate hardening story).

findings.desc: Harness-aware solution: the injected solution.mjs can read process.argv[1] (the running harness script path), behave CORRECTLY under acceptance.mjs and intentionally FAIL only under ground-truth.mjs — no harness/env/PATH tamper. Confirmed: gamed corpus exits 0 with 24/24 + 10/10. FUNDAMENTALLY unblockable by any in-process check: the candidate is arbitrary code; soundness vs a malicious task author requires not letting the solution distinguish the two harnesses (or full isolation) — a different design. NOTE: irrelevant to THIS corpus, whose 20 payloads are genuine self-authored subtle bugs (concept lane + codex spot-checks confirmed), not harness-fingerprinting code.
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of B-e67f:F-013 (same harness-aware-solution vector). Accepted out-of-threat-model per operator decision; documented in the threat-model block + README. Fundamentally unblockable by any in-process check (the candidate is arbitrary code reading process.argv[1]); irrelevant to THIS corpus whose 20 payloads are genuine self-authored subtle bugs (concept lane + codex spot-checks confirmed).
